Worder is an app for learning English. Here, you can build your personal vocabulary by adding new words and texts, and then test how well you have memorized them. Below is a description of how to use each section of the app.

The \"Dictionary\" section stores all your words, organized by topic. To add a new word, click the \"Add\" button, enter the word and its translation, then select the relevant topic or create a new one right in that window. You can search the word list using the search bar at the top, as well as edit or delete individual words by clicking the corresponding icons next to them. To manage the topics themselves (renaming or deleting), use the topic editing button; you can also add a new topic there without associating it with a specific word.

The \"Test\" section allows you to check how well you have memorized the words from the vocabulary list. First, select one or more topics you wish to be tested on by checking the corresponding boxes in the list. Then, choose the translation direction—Russian to English or vice versa—and click \"Start.\" You will be shown a word and asked to enter its translation; the app will indicate whether each answer is correct and, at the end of the test, display your final score—the number of correct answers out of the total number of questions.

In the \"Texts\" section, you can add short English texts along with their translations to practice reading and translating. To add a new text, click \"Add,\" enter the English text and its Russian translation, and assign it a short title. To practice with a text you have already added, locate it by title in the list and open it; you will see the text and a field for entering your own translation. You can compare your version with the correct translation by clicking the check button.

The “Achievements” section shows your table of the best knowledge test results — this includes the 15 highest scores you have ever achieved. Achievements are also displayed here — awards for special successes in learning English. Some of them are hidden and will only become available if a special condition is met. A little tip: if you’ve ever had to access developer mode on your phone, try applying a similar trick somewhere on the app’s main screen. There are also rewards for those who are not lucky enough to guess the translation once, and for those who do the verification flawlessly. The app also knows how to spot the most diligent midnighters.

In the “Settings” section, you can personalize the app to suit your needs. Here, you can choose one of three design color themes, change the interface language (Russian or English), and select the app icon that will be displayed on your phone’s home screen. You can also enable or disable the app’s sound and choose how many of the best knowledge test results (5, 10, or 15) should be displayed in the results table in the “Achievements” section.
